## Overview

With `veg_model = marram`, every grid cell carries the marram grass model of the
[previous vignette](../13_marram_grass/13_marram_grass.md), and the plants and the bed are
coupled both ways:

- **Plants shape the wind.** Each time step, shoot density and canopy height give a frontal
  area. That frontal area becomes the effective cover in AeoLiS's shear reduction,
  `1 / sqrt(1 + gamma_vegshear rhoveg)`. The shoots bend in strong wind, so the cover
  depends on the current wind speed [@LaporteFauret2024; @Walter2012].
- **The bed shapes the plants.** Every `veg_interval` (a day), each cell is advanced using:
  - the rate of bed-level change since the last update, as burial;
  - the fraction of the interval it spent under water;
  - rainfall and evapotranspiration from `veg_water_file`;
  - the day of the year from `refdate`.
- **Plants spread.** Bare cells are colonised from occupied neighbours at about 0.4 m per
  year [@Keijsers2015], with occasional jumps [@Bonte2021].
- **Roots resist waves.** When a storm cuts back the dune, sand in the rooted layer costs
  more of the waves' work to remove than bare sand [@Figlus2014; @DeBattisti2020].

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using Aeolis
using Plots
using Printf
using Random
```

## The beach and its weather

A transect rises from below the low-tide line to a backshore at 3 m, 100 m inland. Beyond
126 m the hinterland is fixed, so the bare sand behind the dune does not blow away. There is
a semidiurnal tide of 1 m. Every day has a new onshore wind: a Weibull speed with a mean of
7 m/s, from directions within 40° of shore-normal. Rain falls on 45 % of days, and potential
evapotranspiration follows the seasons. The weather is drawn from a seeded random number
generator, so the vignette is reproducible.

```{julia}
day = 86400.0
years = 3
rng = Xoshiro(1)
x = collect(0.0:1.0:150.0)
zb0 = @. min(-1.0 + x / 25, 3.0)
nd = 365 * years + 1
td = (0:(nd - 1)) .* day
wind = hcat(td, [7.0 / 0.886 * sqrt(-log(rand(rng))) for _ in td],
            [270.0 + 80 * (rand(rng) - 0.5) for _ in td])
tt = collect(0.0:3600.0:(nd * day))
tide = hcat(tt, sin.(2pi .* tt ./ (12.42 * 3600)))
doy = [(k % 365) + 1 for k in 0:(nd - 1)]
water = hcat(td, [rand(rng) < 0.45 ? -4.9 * log(rand(rng)) : 0.0 for _ in td],
             @. 2.0 - 1.5 * cos(2pi * (doy - 15) / 365))
base = (; xgrid_file=x, bed_file=zb0, ne_file=(@. ifelse(x >= 126, zb0, -10.0)),
        th_nelayer=true, wind_file=wind, tide_file=tide, process_tide=true,
        grain_size=0.0003, dt=3600.0, tstop=years * 365day, output_times=30day,
        refdate="2020-01-01 00:00", process_avalanche=true,
        output_vars=[:zb, :veg_N, :hveg, :rhoveg, :veg_P, :veg_Gb, :veg_zdot])
nothing
```

Marram is planted between 110 and 125 m at 30 % of the density of a closed stand, 141 shoots
per m². The same beach is also run without plants.

```{julia}
planting = @. ifelse(110 <= x <= 125, 0.3, 0.0)
marram = solve(AeolisProblem(AeolisParameters(; base..., process_vegetation=true,
                                              veg_model=:marram, veg_file=planting,
                                              veg_water_file=water)); rng=Xoshiro(2))
bare = solve(AeolisProblem(AeolisParameters(; base...)))
nothing
```

## The dune

```{julia}
z = transect(marram, :zb)
zbare = transect(bare, :zb)
volume(zz) = sum(max.(zz[101:end] .- 3.0, 0.0))     # m³ per m of beach, above 3 m
plt = plot(x, zbare[:, end]; color=:gray, lw=2, label="bare, year 3",
           xlabel="distance (m)", ylabel="bed level (m)", xlims=(80, 150), legend=:topleft)
for (k, c) in zip((13, 25, 37), (:lightgreen, :green, :darkgreen))
    plot!(plt, x, z[:, k]; lw=2, color=c, label="marram, year $((k - 1) ÷ 12)")
end
plot!(plt, x, zb0; color=:black, ls=:dash, label="initial")
plt
```

```{julia}
for k in (13, 25, 37)
    @printf("year %d: dune volume %.1f m³/m with marram, %.1f m³/m bare; crest %.2f m\n",
            (k - 1) ÷ 12, volume(z[:, k]), volume(zbare[:, k]), maximum(z[:, k]))
end
```

The bare beach builds no dune: sand blown off the beach crosses the flat backshore. The
planted strip slows the wind at the bed, traps the sand and grows a dune several metres high
in three years. The wind blows onshore every day here, so this rate is high for a real
coast.

## The plants

```{julia}
N = transect(marram, :veg_N)
months = (0:(size(N, 2) - 1))
heatmap(months, x[95:135], N[95:135, :]; xlabel="months", ylabel="distance (m)",
        colorbar_title="shoots per m²", c=:Greens)
```

Shoot density rises each summer and falls back each winter.

- **Seaward edge:** the stand spreads over the bare beach a little each year, which is as
  much as the front speed allows.
- **Crest:** the stand thins where the dune grows fastest.

The diagnostics at the end of the run show why:

```{julia}
G = transect(marram, :veg_Gb)
zdot = transect(marram, :veg_zdot)
tr = MarramTraits()
for i in 106:4:126
    @printf("x = %3d m: bed %.2f m, burial %5.2f m/season, G_b %.2f, shoots %3.0f per m²\n",
            x[i], z[i, end], zdot[i, end] * Aeolis.season_length(tr), G[i, end], N[i, end])
end
```

Where the crest is buried by about 0.7 m per growing season, more than twice the optimum
[@Nolet2018], the burial multiplier `G_b` falls to about 0.3. Fewer shoots survive there than
on the flanks. The landward edge receives little sand. The model would slowly lower vigour
there through soil-biota pressure, but three years is too short for that to show.

## How densely to plant

The stand is planted at densities from 2 % to 100 % of a closed stand, and run for two years:

```{julia}
for c in (0.02, 0.1, 1.0)
    p = AeolisParameters(; base..., tstop=2 * 365day, output_times=365day,
                         process_vegetation=true, veg_model=:marram,
                         veg_file=(@. ifelse(110 <= x <= 125, c, 0.0)),
                         veg_water_file=water)
    zz = transect(solve(AeolisProblem(p); rng=Xoshiro(2)), :zb)
    @printf("planted at %4.0f %%: dune volume %.1f m³/m after two years\n", 100c,
            volume(zz[:, end]))
end
```

Even a sparse planting builds most of the dune, for two reasons:

- **Shelter saturates.** The drag on full-height marram reaches its cap at about 45 shoots
  per m².
- **Sparse stands fill in.** They grow toward their capacity within a season or two.

@Bonte2021 found that dunes grow fastest at intermediate cover. The model does not reproduce
this, either here or in two-dimensional runs with patchy planting, where dune volume also rose
with the area planted. Why the two differ is not yet understood. The supply of sand, the
measure of dune growth, and how trapping depends on cover in their cellular model are
candidates.

## A storm

After the three years, a storm attacks the dune for two days. A surge of 2.5 m and waves 3 m
high with a 10 s period collide with the dune face, which erodes as in @Palmsten2012.

The storm run starts from the state after three years (`u0`), so the roots are those the dune
grew. It is repeated with the roots made ineffective: a traits file sets the strength of bare
sand, `tau0`, so high that reinforcement adds nothing. The light wind moves no sand.

The dune toe is set at 2.7 m. AeoLiS takes as the toe the point of the profile nearest that
elevation, and the hinterland lies at exactly 3 m.

```{julia}
t0 = years * 365day
storm = (; tstart=t0, tstop=t0 + 2day, output_times=2day,
         wind_file=[0.0 2.0 270.0; 4000day 2.0 270.0], tide_file=[0.0 2.5; 4000day 2.5],
         wave_file=[0.0 3.0 10.0; 4000day 3.0 10.0], process_wave=true, process_runup=true,
         process_dune_erosion=true, dune_toe_elevation=2.7, beach_slope=0.04)
inert = tempname() * ".toml"
write(inert, "tau0 = 1e12\n")
u3 = marram.u
eroded = Dict{String,Float64}()
plt = plot(x, u3.zb[:, 2]; color=:black, lw=2, label="before the storm",
           xlabel="distance (m)", ylabel="bed level (m)", xlims=(90, 135), legend=:topleft)
for (label, kw, c) in (("with roots", (;), :darkgreen), ("roots ineffective", (; veg_traits_file=inert), :orange))
    p = AeolisParameters(; base..., storm..., process_vegetation=true, veg_model=:marram,
                         veg_file=planting, kw...)
    z1 = solve(AeolisProblem(p; u0=u3); rng=Xoshiro(3)).u.zb[:, 2]
    eroded[label] = sum(max.(u3.zb[:, 2] .- z1, 0.0))
    plot!(plt, x, z1; lw=2, color=c, label=label)
end
@printf("eroded: %.1f m³/m with roots, %.1f m³/m without; %.0f %% less\n",
        eroded["with roots"], eroded["roots ineffective"],
        100 * (1 - eroded["with roots"] / eroded["roots ineffective"]))
plt
```

The roots keep a third of the dune face that the storm would otherwise take. Flume
experiments found 8-37 % less erosion with vegetation [@Figlus2014; @Kosmalla2026], and
intact cores of marram 36 % [@DeBattisti2020]. The fine-root fraction of the traits was fitted
to these, and the run falls in their range.

The model does not represent one effect seen in a large flume
[@Feagin2023]: a vegetated dune that eroded faster, because plants changed the run-up and
infiltration of the swash.

## What remains uncertain

- **The burial response and soil-biota pressure** rest on few studies.
- **Root reinforcement:** the tensile strength of marram roots has not been measured, and
  the erosion data constrain only its product with the fine-root fraction.

Both uncertainties are listed with ranges in `marram_info`.
